concept: Real randomness is streakier than it feels: in 100 fair flips, a run of 5+ of the same side happens about 97% of the time.

misconceptions.label: Random means evenly mixed
misconceptions.why_tempting: Long runs look like a pattern, so a 'random' sequence feels like it should keep switching sides.
misconceptions.refutation: Each flip ignores the last one, so switching only half the time is normal. Over 100 flips that makes long runs almost certain.
misconceptions.source_note: People inventing random sequences switch too often (Falk & Konold 1997, via docs/research/showcase-facts.md)

misconceptions.label: A long streak means something's off
misconceptions.why_tempting: Seven heads in a row feels too unlikely to be luck.
misconceptions.refutation: Any single run of 7 is unlikely, but with 100 flips there are dozens of places one can start, so some long run is expected.
misconceptions.source_note: Same computation as the reveal (exact DP in docs/research/showcase-facts.md)

items.prompt: Flip a fair coin 100 times. What's the longest run of the same side in a row?
One of these was flipped, one was made up by a person. Which is the real coin? A: HTHHTHTTHTHHTHTTHTHT  B: HTTTTHHTHHHHTTHTHHHT
